successors.note: Infobox 'succeeded by the Najahids'. The last Ziyadid was murdered in 1018 and replaced by the Ethiopian slave Nafis; Najah, who 'founded the Najahid dynasty in 1022', killed Nafis. The Najahid dossier starts in 1022, so 1018-1021 has no named state.

rulers.name: 'Abdallah or Ziyad ibn Ishaq
rulers.note: The page's 'c. 1012'; al-Husayn ibn Salamah, 'the Mamluk', saved the kingdom from collapse and died in 1012.

rulers.name: Ibrahim or 'Abdallah
rulers.note: A kinsman; the last Ziyadid, murdered in 1018.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 819-865, which Cliopatria lacks (its row starts 866): Muhammad ibn Ziyad 'arrived there in 818' and 'won control over the Tihama lowland in the next year'; infobox 'Established: 819'. No area on the page.

correction.text: Tihama with Aden and the maritime provinces as far north as Hali, holding 866-1018

keyframe_review.note: 215.4 thousand km2 (Yemen with Najran, east to Hadramawt) for 866-1039 in one polygon. The infobox gives no area. The page shows the Ziyadids as lords of the Tihama; Umara lists their possessions as 'Aden and the maritime provinces as far north as Hali' and 'Najran, and Bayhan in the highlands'; the highlands were governed by Abbasid governors to 847 and then by the Yu'firids, who 'forced the Ziyadid ruler to tolerate their rule in exchange for mentioning him on coins'. The direct state is the Tihama with the Aden coast; the highlands and Hadramawt are the Yu'firid vassal tint (ledger 847). The shape also ends in 1018, not 1039.

correction.text: no Ziyadid land in 1040-1055: the Tihama of Zabid belongs to the Najahids (najahid-dynasty)

This 215.4 thousand km2 polygon is the all-Yemen union that Cliopatria also gives to the Najahids from 1066; use the najahid-dynasty dossier.

region.text: Tihama, the Red Sea lowland of Yemen

ledger.note: 819: Muhammad ibn Ziyad founds Zabid and holds the Tihama. He 'arrived there in 818', 'won control over the Tihama lowland in the next year' and 'established a new city, Zabid, as his capital'; infobox 'Established: 819'. He kept 'recognizing Abbasid overlordship'.

region.text: Sanaa, Janad and Hadramawt, the Yu'firid lands

ledger.note: 847: the Yu'firids take Sanaa but defer to Zabid. 'The Yufirids established an independent state in San'a in 847 and forced the Ziyadid ruler to tolerate their rule in exchange for mentioning him on coins' (Ziyadid page); the Yu'firid page: Muhammad 'ruled over Saana, Janad and Hadramawt but paid formal deference to the Ziyadid dynasty'. The page does not call this vassalage; Yu'firids also 'nominally acknowledged the suzerainty of the Abbasid caliphs'.

region.text: Sanaa, Janad and Hadramawt, the Yu'firid lands

ledger.note: 989: the Yu'firids burn Zabid. The Yu'firid page: they 'successfully attacked the Ziyadids in 989, investing and plundering Zabid' and the Ziyadid page 'again attacked in 989 and burnt Zabid'; the end of the formal deference is bridged from the attack (the Yu'firid dynasty ends in 997).

region.text: Tihama with Aden and the maritime provinces as far north as Hali

ledger.note: 1018: the last Ziyadid is murdered and the dynasty ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1018'; 'the last Ziyadi ruler was murdered in 1018 and replaced by Nafis' (Salibi); the Najahid page: 'The last Ziyadid king died in 1018, leaving a child behind' with the regency to 'his Abyssinian administers Nafis and Najah'. Najah later killed Nafis and founded the Najahid dynasty in 1022.

wars.name: Qarmatian sack of Zabid
wars.outcome: 'Zabid itself was sacked by the sectarian Qarmatians' in 904; no territorial change recorded.

wars.name: Yu'firid attack on Zabid
wars.outcome: The Yu'firids invested and plundered Zabid in 989; no territorial change recorded.

certainty.note: The Tihama coastline is firm; the highland and Hadramawt edges, and the Aden-to-Hali coast, are approximate and no page gives a boundary.

notes: Cliopatria's Ziyadid row (866..1138, six shapes) is two rows in one: the first shape (866-1039, 215.4 thousand km2) is an all-Yemen polygon that is also the Najahid row's first shape, and the later shapes (1040-1138) are Najahid/Sulayhid-era land, since the dynasty ended in 1018 (infobox, and the Najahid page). The dossier therefore runs 819-1018 with one adjusted keyframe, one new one for 819-865, and five 'wrong' verdicts. The Najahid dossier by another agent reaches the same view about the Najahid shapes. The infobox has no area, so no comparison was possible. Cliopatria's relations 'Allegiance of Ziyadid dynasty to Abbasid Caliphate 866-946' and 'alliance with the Samanid Empire 886-999' are not on any page opened (the page says only that the rulers kept 'reciting the khutba in the name of the Abbasids' after 866; no Samanid contact is mentioned); the Abbasid dossier by another agent holds the 866-946 vassal events. Unsettled: the extent of Hadramawt influence ('He was able to expand his influence into Hadramawt', undated); the Yu'firid deference (undated within 847-989); 1018-1021 (Nafis's regime) has no named state; the Zaydi imam al-Hadi's base in the northern highlands (897) and the Ismaili conquest of Sanaa (905) are Yu'firid history and not drawn here. Not opened (page budget 5; three used): Zabid, Abu'l-Jaysh Ishaq, Husayn ibn Salama.
